_about: Time-boxed or standing offers worth money to someone paying for LLM inference. Each entry says what, for whom, until when, where it was seen, and how well it was verified. `verified` = checked on the provider's own page on the date in `source`; `unconfirmed` = reported by a third party and the first-party page could not confirm it (kept, labelled); `asserted` = unchecked third-party report, must not ship. Expired entries stay (with `expires` in the past) so the feed can show what was missed. `monitors.json` lists the Context.dev page monitors that watch the pricing pages these entries cite; `pnpm sweep` prints what changed. Updated via PR.

deals.title: Max plans include monthly Claude API credits: $100 on 5x, $200 on 20x
deals.detail: Max 5x $100/month, Max 20x $200/month; Team $20 per Standard seat and $100 per Premium seat pooled to $500. Claim once on claude.ai (web): Settings > Billing > API credits > link a Console org. New subscribers wait 7 days on the plan. Credits expire at the end of each billing cycle, no rollover. Covers the Claude API, Managed Agents, Agent SDK and the Console playground; does not cover Claude Code or extra usage in the Claude apps. The link cannot be changed without support.
deals.source: platform.claude.com docs 'API credits for Max and Team plans', read 29 Oct 2026

deals.title: Gemini 4 Argon launch pricing ends 30 Nov: $2/$10 becomes $4/$20 per 1M
deals.detail: Gemini 4 Argon standard tier is $2.00 input / $10.00 output through 30 Nov 2026 and doubles to $4.00 / $20.00 on 1 Dec (batch and flex $1/$5 → $2/$10, context caching $0.10 → $0.20). Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.6 Flash are $0.75 / $3.75 through 31 Dec, then $1.50 / $7.50 on 1 Jan 2027 (caching $0.075 → $0.15). Front-load eval and batch work before the step.
deals.source: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, read 29 Oct 2026 (earlier figures from a 28 Oct search excerpt were wrong and are corrected here)

deals.title: Gemini API free tier: 3.8 Flash and 3.6 Flash at $0, prompts used to improve Google products
deals.detail: Free tier gives free input and output tokens on Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.6 Flash, the Flash TTS models and Robotics ER 2. Gemini 4 Argon is not on the free tier. Rate limits are lower than paid; see the rate-limits page.
deals.data_terms: Free-tier prompts and responses are used to improve Google's products. Paid tier content is not.

deals.title: Three new :free models on OpenRouter this month
deals.detail: nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free (1M context, 15 Oct), xingchen-agi/xing4.0-29b-a4b:free (262K, 16 Oct), recursive/flint-v1.0:free (262K, 21 Oct). Free-model limits: 20 requests/min; 50/day with under $10 of credits ever bought, 1,000/day at $10 or more.
deals.data_terms: NVIDIA-hosted free models may train on prompts; check each listing's data policy.

deals.title: stealth/glyph-cluster free on Vercel AI Gateway during its stealth period (256K context)
deals.detail: Anonymous preview model, free while in stealth since 7 Oct 2026. Early access is limited to Pro or Enterprise teams that have bought AI Gateway credits. No Zero Data Retention. Text in, function calling yes, structured outputs no.
deals.data_terms: Prompts and responses may be retained and used for training and model improvement.

deals.title: stealth/glyph-cluster reported free via Kilo Code since 27 Oct
deals.detail: Third-party catalogs list the same stealth model free in Kilo Code at about 200 requests/hour. Kilo's leaderboard shows it in heavy use but its blog has no post for it and the model page 404s, so the free terms are unconfirmed. The Vercel AI Gateway listing of the same model is confirmed (see the vercel entry).
deals.source: freellm.net and custom.typingmind.com listings; kilo.ai/leaderboard checked 29 Oct 2026 (no first-party terms found)
deals.data_terms: Stealth program default: prompts and completions may be used to train and evaluate the model.

deals.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free on OpenCode Zen, zero retention, for a limited time
deals.detail: OpenCode Zen lists a separate 'DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free' model at $0 input/output/cached, 'free on OpenCode for a limited time' (reported since 15 Oct 2026). The paid entry is $0.30 / $1.20. Press reports cap the free one at 200K context; the page does not say. Nine other free models are listed too (GLM-5.3-Flash Free, Beam Free, Flint 40B Free, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Free, Jev 1.13 Free and more).
deals.data_terms: Zero retention, not used for training (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free is not on the exceptions list). Big Pickle, Flint 40B Free, MiMo Free and the NVIDIA-hosted Nemotron free models ARE exceptions and may train on prompts.

deals.title: Qoder: DeepSeek-Flash (V4.1-Flash-1017) at 0 credits within a daily allowance until 31 Oct
deals.detail: From 20 Oct 2026 the model's credit rate is 0.0x instead of 0.1x inside a per-day allowance (larger for paid plans), including at maximum reasoning effort. Ends 31 Oct 24:00 Singapore time (UTC+8), extended from 24 Oct. Individual plans only (Free, Lite, Pro, Pro+, Ultra); Teams and Enterprise excluded. No claim needed. After the allowance, the normal credit rate applies.

deals.title: Qoder: claim 100 credits a day in the desktop app
deals.detail: Since 18 Sep 2026, individual accounts (free and paid) can claim 100 credits every day from the gift icon in the Usage panel. Manual claim, no catch-up for missed days, each claim valid 30 days. End date 'to be announced'. Teams and Enterprise excluded.

deals.title: DeepSeek Search and Fetch API free via Claude Code, Codex or DeepSeek Harness until 1 Nov
deals.detail: Server-side Search/Fetch calls made through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code or Codex are free; per-request billing of $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests (each API) starts 00:00 Beijing time on 1 Nov 2026. Failed requests, empty results and timeouts are never billed.

deals.title: DeepSeek API off-peak: 50% off outside 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC weekdays
deals.detail: deepseek-flash (V4.1-Flash-1017) is $0.15 / $0.60 per 1M off-peak vs $0.30 / $1.20 peak; deepseek-v4-pro $0.66 / $1.98 vs $1.32 / $3.96 (cache hits $0.003 / $0.022 off-peak). Peak is 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC Monday to Friday excluding Chinese public holidays; everything else, including weekends, is off-peak. Schedule batch and eval jobs accordingly.

deals.title: Novita batch inference at an introductory 50% off
deals.detail: 'Batch inference is available at an introductory 50% discount on input and output tokens for supported models.' No end date and no model list on the pricing page; the batch API guide lists supported models. Worth it for eval runs and backfills on open models.

deals.title: Fireworks: region-restricted on-demand deployments cost 1.5x
deals.detail: A price increase, not a deal: 'Region-restricted deployments are priced at a 1.5x premium' under on-demand deployments. The page does not say this applies to serverless, and gives no start date (an earlier report said 1 Sep and 'serverless'; neither is on the page). If you pinned a region on an on-demand Fireworks deployment, re-check the rate.

deals.title: Fireworks: Muse Glimmer 30B SFT free via UI and Serverless Training API until 30 Nov, no card
deals.detail: 'Muse Glimmer 30B SFT is free via UI and Serverless Training API until 11/30. No credit card required.' Fine-tuning runs on this model, not serverless inference. The page also marks Qwen3 8B embeddings at $0.10 per 1M input as a limited-time offer with no end date.

deals.title: Cerebras: one-time $5 credit when you add a payment method, expires in 30 days
deals.detail: 'Add a valid payment method to receive a one-time $5 promotional credit.' 'The credit expires 30 days after activation.' No automatic charges; API and Playground access pause when the credit is used up or expires unless you buy pay-as-you-go credits. Development and evaluation only, not production. The no-card free tier reportedly ended in Aug 2026.

deals.title: Claude Batch API: 50% off input and output on every model
deals.detail: Asynchronous; most batches finish within 1 hour, results available within 24h. Batch prices: Fable 5.1 $5/$25, Opus 5.5 $2/$10, Sonnet 5.5 $1/$5, Haiku 5.5 $0.05/$0.25 per 1M. Stacks with prompt caching. Also exposed on OpenRouter as :batch variants at the same prices. The lever for evals, backfills and anything not interactive.
deals.source: platform.claude.com docs batch-processing and pricing pages, read 29 Oct 2026; OpenRouter /models :batch prices same day

deals.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash free on OpenRouter for 72 hours (19–22 Oct)
deals.detail: The stealth model 'Space Bunny' returned as MiniMax M3.1 Flash, free for 72h from 19 Oct, then $0.15/$0.60 per 1M. OpenRouter's catalog shows minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash created 19 Oct 2026 at exactly that price.
deals.source: OpenRouter and MiniMax on X, 19 Oct 2026; openrouter.ai/api/v1/models re-checked 29 Oct 2026
